q: Does Germany's supply chain law make buyers ask suppliers for climate data?
title: German supply chain law and climate data
short: Not directly. The German supply chain act focuses on human rights and a short list of environmental harms, not greenhouse gases. Climate questions usually come from the buyer's own targets, CSRD reporting or CBAM. Answer both in one place, because the same procurement team often sends them together.
audience: Suppliers in India, Bangladesh, Pakistan and Vietnam receiving questionnaires from German customers

sections.h: Where the climate questions come from
ul: Science based or net zero targets that include Scope 3.
Sustainability reporting under the CSRD, for companies still in scope after the 2026 simplification.

p: Scope 1 and 2 by site with sources, product footprints if asked, and a contact for follow up. Keep the human rights answers in the format the buyer's risk analysis needs.

senseible: Senseible reads your electricity bills and fuel invoices into Scope 1 and 2 records with the factor and source on each line, the site data a buyer questionnaire starts from. It does not produce verified product footprints or fill a buyer's portal for you.
